metadata.key_test: Tier 2 (legal/constitutional suppression) outcome -- predicted to fall 'between' Tier 1 and Tier 3; Mod9 (re-suppression after porosity) test; Mod10 (Article 155 backstop + accommodation on the 1978 autonomy system).
metadata.notes: Run4 Case 16. WGI cited on World Bank estimate scale (-2.5 to +2.5). Spain's P1 is high but distinctly lower than Germany/UK/Belgium -- relevant to tier choice. Most pillar values ordinal/estimated, not cardinal.

pre_event.event_description: October 2017 Catalan independence referendum, met by Tier 2 legal/constitutional suppression rather than military force or Tier-3 expanded porosity.

context.backstop_details: Spain's 1978 autonomy system IS porosity-with-backstop (Mod10), with Article 155 (direct rule, ~Oct 2017-June 2018) as the backstop briefly deployed and then withdrawn, followed by accommodation (pardons 2021, amnesty law 2024, fiscal dialogue).

data_gaps: regional_antisystem_vote (pro-independence vote share at 2017 not given as a single figure)
Spain (Catalonia).notes: Spain WGI estimate scale: RoL 0.82, GE 0.75 -- high but clearly below Germany/UK/Belgium. Catalonia ~18.8-20% of Spanish GDP; GDP per capita EUR37,426 (2024), above the Spanish average. Suppression mechanism: Article 155 + Constitutional Court action + prosecutions/exile (Puigdemont); some Oct 1 police violence but no sustained deployment.

a_trajectory_ranking.basis: High-but-lower P1 + Tier 2 legal suppression on the 1978 autonomy system.

b_violence.prediction: Minimal violence (brief police clashes on Oct 1); no sustained deployment.

c_convergence.prediction: Secession pressure de-escalates following Article 155 + accommodation.
c_convergence.basis: Pardons (2021) + amnesty (2024) + fiscal dialogue layered on autonomy.

d_failure_dimension.prediction: Legal/constitutional dimension is the stress surface, not military or institutional collapse.

f_reversal_risk.prediction: N/A -- not a democratic-transition reversal case.

g_suppression_mechanism.classification: Tier 2 (legal/constitutional suppression): Article 155 direct rule, Constitutional Court action, prosecutions/exile. Framework predicts Tier 2 falls 'between' Tier 1 (delays without reducing pressure) and Tier 3 (reduces without eliminating).
g_suppression_mechanism.falsification_condition: Mechanism is military (Tier 1) or expanded porosity (Tier 3); or pressure neither delayed nor reduced.

h_substate_turbulence.prediction: High separatist pressure (Catalonia ~19% of GDP) managed via Article 155 backstop + accommodation; Mod9 (re-suppression after porosity -> worse outcomes) not expected to be confirmed -- Article 155 too mild and brief to be a real test.
h_substate_turbulence.falsification_condition: Pressure escapes the backstop and produces secession or violence.

Spain (Catalonia).outcome_summary: Spain survives, no territorial loss, minimal violence. Pressure de-escalated clearly -- arguably more than a pure 'between' result. Mechanism was Article 155 (temporary backstop) plus subsequent accommodation (pardons, amnesty, fiscal dialogue) layered on the 1978 autonomy system. Secession vote collapsed: pro-independence bloc fell below a majority for the first time since 1980.
key_events: Article 155 direct rule ~Oct 2017-June 2018; Constitutional Court action; prosecutions/exile (Puigdemont)
May 2024 regional election: pro-union Socialists (PSC) won for the first time -- 42 of 135 seats, 27.96%; first time Socialists led in both votes and seats in Catalan history
Pro-independence bloc fell to 61 of 135 seats (68 needed) -- below a majority for the first time since 1980
CEO polling: ~50% against independence, ~42% for; drought (not secession) the leading public concern

analysis.overall_assessment: Confirmed: Spain survives with no territorial loss and minimal violence. Tier 2 legal suppression produced a discrete suppression episode followed by accommodation; pressure reduced more than the predicted 'between' result. Suggestively, the one case reaching for legal coercion is also the lowest-P1 of the three porosity cases (ordinally suggestive, not proven).
safeguards_triggered: I (porosity-with-backstop, Mod10: Article 155 backstop + 1978 autonomy + accommodation)
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Tier 2 legal/constitutional suppression layered onto a porosity-with-backstop autonomy system can REDUCE secession pressure more than a pure 'between' prediction when followed by accommodation rather than sustained re-suppression.
proposed_framework_modifications: Mod9 remains unproven -- needs a genuine sustained, hard re-suppression case (Catalonia is a weak/null test, not a confirmation or refutation).
Promote candidate Safeguard I (porosity-with-backstop) to a working safeguard.
analysis.baseline_impact: No modification adopted from this case; Mod9 still needs a proper test before any baseline-affecting change.
analysis.strict_recode_note: Strict re-code applied per run6 (post-hoc d-dimension -> PARTIAL; narrow-gap a-trajectory annotated with Mod4). Honest aggregate target ~62-78%.
